turns.content: Four active galaxies lie at about 1, 7, 70, and 700 Mpc, and their spectra cover the Sloan i band. State the rest wavelength of H-alpha and outline how to determine which spectrum contains the line.
Estimate the redshift at each distance with z approximately H0*d/c, taking H0=70 km/s/Mpc and c=3.0e5 km/s.
Use lambda_obs=lambda_0(1+z) to calculate the observed H-alpha wavelength for each galaxy.
Compare those wavelengths with the Sloan i-band coverage and identify the in-band case.
Which galaxy is therefore best suited for measuring the H-alpha profile?
How sensitive is that selection to modest changes in the Hubble constant within the same linear approximation?
Summarize the four calculated wavelengths using lambda_0=6562.8 Angstrom and approximate i-band coverage of 7000-8500 Angstrom.
What limitations follow from the approximate passband edges and linear Hubble-law treatment?
State the selected distance class under this calculation.
Give an appropriate confidence qualification rather than treating the approximate inputs as exact.
Report the adopted H0, wavelength comparison, selected galaxy, and qualification.
